ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">Are organizations dedicating enough people to their content initiatives? When we asked B2B marketers how content marketing work gets done within their organizations, most (76%) have a dedicated content marketing team or person on staff. And the larger the organization, the more likely it was to have dedicated resources.</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">But most (54%) who have a dedicated content marketing team or staff say the team is small, consisting of two to five people.</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><img data-component="image" class="ContentParagraph-Image" there’s no dedicated team or person?" style="scroll-margin-top:10rem;scroll-snap-margin-top:10rem">What if there’s no dedicated team or person?</h3><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">Believe it or not, 24% of B2B respondents say they </span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"><span class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_italic">don’t </span></span><span When we asked that group how the work gets done, 50% say they rely on multiple content teams (e.g., department, brand, or product), 7% say they use an outside content marketing agency/vendor, and 43% list “other.”</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">Those who chose “other” offered explanations that ranged from two people with multiple responsibilities, including content, to whoever was available.</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">And therein lies a problem: While staff may handle content-related tasks, no one is responsible for </span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"><a class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_link" target="_self" href="https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/content-operations/how-to-unite-roles-and-teams-and-scale-your-content-operations">leading content marketing as a strategic approach</a></span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">. Here’s what she says:</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><br/></p><div data-component="embeds"><div data-type="raw-html"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><colgroup data-width="1035"><col style="width:33.1401%"><col style="width:66.8599%"></colgroup><tbody><tr><td><img width="175" alt="ann-handley-230x230.jpg" src="https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt663d10211b43b0ca/blt2b1a5422ea2f8637/67a0dd5d18aae903f2cc847f/ann-handley-230x230.jpg" height="174" style="width: 175;height: 174;"><p>Ann Handley</p><p>Chief Content Officer</p><p>MarketingProfs</p></td><td><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>My question is ... how are you measuring this?</em><em><br italic="[object Object]"></em><em>Or, rather, how do you know it's not creating the action you want to inspire?</em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>B2B content is part of a complex matrix of various touchpoints, seen and unseen, including word of mouth, dark social, that one guy who mentioned your brand on LinkedIn.</em><em><br italic="[object Object]"></em><em>We want to believe the purchase journey is a straight, orderly line of attribution:</em><em><br italic="[object Object]"></em><em>Read blog post. > Hit demo. > Buy.</em></span></p><br><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text"><span class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_italic">But B2B — or any marketing — doesn't work that way. It’s less straight line, more squiggly scribble that overlaps in oddball ways. Less straightforward path; more conspiratorial crime scene investigation board.</span></span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><br/></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text"><span class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_italic">What marketers can do about it is to rethink the messy muddle of attribution to think about more meaningful ways to know what's ‘working.’</span></span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><br/></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text"><span class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_italic">Not how many people downloaded a white paper ... but how many then signed up for your email newsletter? And then, how many of them wrote back to you when you told a story in the last issue about a specific problem they have? What did existing customers tell you worked the last time you spoke with them? Rethink off-the-shelf metrics (because there is no shelf).</span></span></p></blockquote></div><h3 class="ContentText ContentText_variant_h3 ContentText_align_left" data-testid="content-text" id="Other content creation challenges" style="scroll-margin-top:10rem;scroll-snap-margin-top:10rem">Other content creation challenges</h3><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">Last year, most B2B marketers (57%) cited creating the right content for the audience as a challenge. This year, only 40% did. That may indicate that B2B marketers have improved or focused more on crafting </span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"><a class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_link" target="_self" href="https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/content-marketing-strategy/why-data-driven-personalization-is-still-so-hard-and-how-to-make-it-easier">better-targeted content</a></span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"> in the last 12 months.</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">Fewer marketers mention differentiating content and creating it consistently as top challenges this year compared to last (43% and 42%, respectively, this year, down from 54% for both last year).</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">Creating enough content is still a challenge for 39% this year. Last year, we distinguished between creating enough content to keep up with internal demand (34%) and external demand (30%). Content repurposing is a challenge for 37%. As it was a new option this year, a comparison is not available.</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">And here’s a somewhat surprising change given </span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"><a class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_link" target="_self" href="https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/seo-for-content/how-to-survive-3-new-threats-to-your-seo-strategy">recent SEO developments</a></span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">: Only 35% of marketers cite optimizing for SEO as a top challenge this year, down from 45% last year. Perhaps even more surprising? Only 27% said creating quality content is a challenge, down from 44% last year.</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><img data-component="image" class="ContentParagraph-Image" data-src="https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt663d10211b43b0ca/blt3e28281ad01f49cb/67a0dd93868de7607693b3c9/b2b-research-content-creation-challenges-768x503.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale" src="https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt663d10211b43b0ca/blt3e28281ad01f49cb/67a0dd93868de7607693b3c9/b2b-research-content-creation-challenges-768x503.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale" loading="lazy" alt="b2b-research-content-creation-challenges-768x503.jpg" title="b2b-research-content-creation-challenges-768x503.jpg"/></p><h3 class="ContentText ContentText_variant_h3 ContentText_align_left" data-testid="content-text" id="B2B marketers’ tech stacks lack these essentials" style="scroll-margin-top:10rem;scroll-snap-margin-top:10rem">B2B marketers’ tech stacks lack these essentials</h3><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">When we asked B2B marketers which capabilities, if any, are missing from their marketing tech stack, nearly half (47%) say they lack efficient lead generation and nurturing processes. Most look only at the distribution costs alone.</em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>It takes time to create content — whether the hours you pay an agency or your in-house team, their time costs money. That means they are only calculating a portion of their content investment.</em></span></p><br><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></blockquote></div><h2 class="ContentText ContentText_variant_h2 ContentText_align_left" data-testid="content-text" id="AI use trends" style="scroll-margin-top:10rem;scroll-snap-margin-top:10rem">AI use trends</h2><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">When it comes to </span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"><a class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_link" target="_self" href="https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/ai-content-creation-tools/experts-reveal-the-worst-and-best-advice-on-using-generative-ai-in-content-marketing">AI use in B2B content marketing</a></span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">, we found many marketers experimenting, but few incorporate it into daily operations. Podcasts produce media-rich and engaging content that performs well across multiple channels, including social media, blogs, and newsletters.</em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>Like other content marketing, tracking direct attribution from podcast engagement to closed deals is hard. The way podcasts are consumed makes measurement that much more difficult.</em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>Under pressure to show ROI, valuable marketing programs like podcasts get cut due to imprecise measurement. And marketers often focus on the wrong KPIs for podcasts.</em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><a href="https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/content-marketing-strategy/how-to-achieve-business-podcasting-success-and-pitfalls-to-avoid"><em>Podcasting for business</em></a></span><span data-everlit-voice="68" class="everlit-audio"><em> should be viewed as a content engine and a relationship builder. Traditional metrics miss both. Businesses don’t need a large podcast audience — they need the right audience. So, instead of tracking downloads and subscribers, they should measure content engagement, brand mentions, lead generation, and business relationships.</em></span></p><br><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></blockquote></div><h3 class="ContentText ContentText_variant_h3 ContentText_align_left" class="Blockquote-Quote"><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text">So, how can B2B content and marketing teams act on these benchmarks and trends? I asked CMI's </span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text"><a class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_link" target="_blank" href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/robrose/">Robert Rose</a></span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text"> to provide some advice. Here's what he said:</span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text">“Do. Or do not. There is no try.” </span><br/><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNoneStyle" data-testid="content-text">—  Yoda </span></p><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><br/></p><div data-component="embeds"><div data-type="raw-html"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><colgroup data-width="1035"><col style="width:33.1401%"><col style="width:66.8599%"></colgroup><tbody><tr><td><img width="175" alt="Robert-Rose-Fractional-Marketing-Leader-230x230.png" src="https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt663d10211b43b0ca/blt745c6d7fa35b506a/67a0e2afe5f16c1f0c311aac/Robert-Rose-Fractional-Marketing-Leader-230x230.png" height="174" style="width: 175;height: 174;"><p>Robert Rose</p><p>Chief Strategy Advisor</p><p>Content Marketing Institute</p></td><td><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>One of the more common situations I see B2B marketing teams facing today is the perennial state of “fixing things.” The CMS never got fully implemented. The “phase </em></span><span data-everlit-voice="126" data-everlit-no-audio="true" class="everlit-audio  no-audio"><em>X</em></span><span data-everlit-voice="126" data-everlit-audio-only="true" class="everlit-audio audio-only"><em></em></span><span data-everlit-voice="126" class="everlit-audio"><em>” of marketing automation doesn’t work the way it should. Customer data is inaccessible. So are the analytics. The new CMO is reorganizing and auditing the teams. Everyone’s struggling to keep up with content demand, so we’re trying to fix our production tools. And we’re all busy experimenting with AI. </em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>On many teams, 100% of time and resources go to fixing or maintaining things. When new ideas come along, the team either can’t do them or sighs wearily and says, “OK, we’ll try.” </em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>But the most successful teams don’t try. They do these things: </em></span></p><br><ul class="wp-block-list"><li><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>Create a content orchestration approach. Fixing the communication, collaboration, and alignment among the teams handling content creation, consumption, publishing, and measurement isn’t glamorous. Still, here’s a truth about one company that now seems to effortlessly produce compelling content that wins all the awards. It once spent years tackling the non-glamorous work of creating cross-team governance, workflows, and standards. It was tough and messy, and it required a shift in working habits. Today, it's operating on an entirely different level. </em></span><p></p><br></li><li><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>Take a structured approach to content and marketing innovations. Letting every team member experiment with AI and other innovations is like setting dogs or cats loose in a pet food store to find a workable approach to better animal nutrition. You won’t get efficiency by adding “experiment” t</em></span><span data-everlit-voice="126" class="everlit-audio"><em>o everyone’s workload or by filling every spare moment</em></span><span data-everlit-voice="126" class="everlit-audio"><em> with a “making marketing better” meeting. Instead, come together (see previous point) to collaborate on and commit to a few strategic bets. They might still fail, but you'll learn why they failed rather than just saying, “We didn’t give it enough resources.” </em></span><p></p><br></li><li><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em><strong>Stop doing some things. </strong></em><em>Many marketing challenges are caused by institutional momentum. One company I worked with created 250 PDFs for thought leadership in a year — only 63 of them earned more than 20 downloads. Teams increasingly focus on task-based outputs rather than meaningful outcomes. Stop producing what doesn’t work, end activities that don't contribute to targeted outcomes, and quit measuring what doesn’t align with overall objectives. </em></span><p></p><br></li></ul><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>Marketing teams must let go of the mindset that being 100% busy is a good thing. It isn’t. There will always be things to fix and maintain. But the only way out of meh content and marketing results isn’t to seek new resources to supplement the repair and maintenance work. </em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>To be remarkable, you must create space for the possibility of creating something remarkable. </em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>As I’ve said to many clients in the last six months, the decisions you make are not nearly as important as making them.</em></span></p><br><p><span data-everlit-voice="7" class="everlit-audio"><em>Stop trying things. Do things. </em></span></p><br><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></blockquote></div><h2 class="ContentText ContentText_variant_h2 ContentText_align_left" data-testid="content-text" id="Methodology" style="scroll-margin-top:10rem;scroll-snap-margin-top:10rem">Methodology</h2><p class="ContentParagraph ContentParagraph_align_left" data-testid="content-paragraph"><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text">The 15</span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"><sup class="ContentText-BodyTextChunk ContentText-BodyTextChunk_superscript">th</sup></span><span class="ContentText ContentText_variant_bodyNormal" data-testid="content-text"> annual content marketing survey was conducted by Content Marketing Institute and MarketingProfs. The survey was fielded between June 25 and Aug. 16, 2024, and was sponsored by The MX Group. The survey drew 1,186 global responses. The “phase \u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"126\\\" data-everlit-no-audio=\\\"true\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio  no-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eX\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"126\\\" data-everlit-audio-only=\\\"true\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio audio-only\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003e\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"126\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003e” of marketing automation doesn’t work the way it should. Customer data is inaccessible. So are the analytics. The new CMO is reorganizing and auditing the teams. Everyone’s struggling to keep up with content demand, so we’re trying to fix our production tools. And we’re all busy experimenting with AI.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eOn many teams, 100% of time and resources go to fixing or maintaining things. When new ideas come along, the team either can’t do them or sighs wearily and says, “OK, we’ll try.”\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eBut the most successful teams don’t try. They do these things:\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cul class=\\\"wp-block-list\\\"\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eCreate a content orchestration approach. Fixing the communication, collaboration, and alignment among the teams handling content creation, consumption, publishing, and measurement isn’t glamorous. Still, here’s a truth about one company that now seems to effortlessly produce compelling content that wins all the awards. It once spent years tackling the non-glamorous work of creating cross-team governance, workflows, and standards. It was tough and messy, and it required a shift in working habits. Today, it\u0026apos;s operating on an entirely different level.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eTake a structured approach to content and marketing innovations. Letting every team member experiment with AI and other innovations is like setting dogs or cats loose in a pet food store to find a workable approach to better animal nutrition. You won’t get efficiency by adding “experiment” t\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"126\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eo everyone’s workload or by filling every spare moment\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"126\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003e with a “making marketing better” meeting. Instead, come together (see previous point) to collaborate on and commit to a few strategic bets. They might still fail, but you\u0026apos;ll learn why they failed rather than just saying, “We didn’t give it enough resources.”\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStop doing some things. \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/em\u003e\u003cem\u003eMany marketing challenges are caused by institutional momentum. One company I worked with created 250 PDFs for thought leadership in a year — only 63 of them earned more than 20 downloads. Teams increasingly focus on task-based outputs rather than meaningful outcomes. Stop producing what doesn’t work, end activities that don\u0026apos;t contribute to targeted outcomes, and quit measuring what doesn’t align with overall objectives.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eMarketing teams must let go of the mindset that being 100% busy is a good thing. It isn’t. There will always be things to fix and maintain. But the only way out of meh content and marketing results isn’t to seek new resources to supplement the repair and maintenance work.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eTo be remarkable, you must create space for the possibility of creating something remarkable.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eAs I’ve said to many clients in the last six months, the decisions you make are not nearly as important as making them.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan data-everlit-voice=\\\"7\\\" class=\\\"everlit-audio\\\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eStop trying things. Do things.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\u003c/tr\u003e\u003c/tbody\u003e\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\",{\"_115\":956,\"_746\":3166,\"_750\":3167},{\"_748\":749,\"_958\":959},[3168],{\"_115\":753,\"_753\":1086},{\"_115\":745,\"_746\":3170,\"_750\":3171},{\"_748\":749},[3172,3174,3179],{\"_115\":753,\"_753\":3173},\"The 15\",{\"_115\":753,\"_756\":3175,\"_753\":3178},[3176],{\"_115\":3177},\"superscript\",\"th\",{\"_115\":753,\"_753\":3180},\" annual content marketing survey was conducted by Content Marketing Institute and MarketingProfs.
